commit_scope: The pulse pile-up was never a respawn: the native dispatcher forks one handler per connection and a public read of /pulse or /pulse/history computes for tens of seconds, so bots at the edge multiplied children until the API starved. Pulse now admits two in-flight requests at Traefik; the API's health probe waits 10 s with 5 retries instead of flapping at 5 s under the host's 60 % steal.
evidence_refs: After #4141 rolled out (manual roll-forward, 2026-10-26 ~05:00 UTC), pulse's `http.bml` process count still rose by one per round (2 → 4 in 70 s) at 748 % CPU and the deploy's API-stability step failed again. A probe BML run inside the pulse image (default seccomp and unconfined) showed host_wait answering nothing() while a child lives and 137 after a kill, so the -2 path of #4141 never fires; the memory note's respawn diagnosis was inferred, not observed.

docker top on a running pulse showed exactly one listener owned by main.bml after three idle rounds; the extra `http.bml` processes are children of the listener — `native-socket-dispatch.bml` nsd-begin forks one handler per accepted connection (nps-fork), and the child's argv is the listener's. strace of one child (26 s old, 19 % CPU): 195 syscalls in 3 s, re-reading a 166-byte FormPersistentSequence block — CPU-bound inside fkwu, i.e. the read path itself (read.bml takes the persistence lock through nw-locked, ws-care commits, read-view renders) costs seconds per request; dir-lock waiters back off at most 32 ms. Connections came from Traefik (172.19.0.1), i.e. public hits on pulse.coherencycoin.com.

Heal at the edge: dcc-pulse in deployment_compose_care.bml adds traefik.http.middlewares.pulse-inflight.inflightreq.amount=2 and attaches it to the pulse and pulse-web routers, so at most two handlers compute at once and the rest answer 429; `./fkwu --check` passes. The API's HEALTHCHECK goes from 5 s/3 retries to 10 s/5 retries (the 5 s probe timed out under steal and restarted a healthy API 142 times on 2026-10-23); test_api_dockerfile_contract follows.

Named, not done: the pulse read path's own cost — a per-round snapshot of /pulse/now and /pulse/health served without the lock, and a dir-lock backoff cap above 32 ms in the kernel — proposed as its own task.

Proof after rollout: pulse http.bml count stays ≤ 3 (listener + 2 children) under load, the deploy's stability step passes and stamps the revision, API healthy with idle CPU between requests, app.hati.earth 200, the malformed entry_key probe answers 422.
